16:96.ar: مَا عِندَكُمۡ يَنفَدُ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَاقࣲۗ وَلَنَجۡزِيَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُوٓاْ أَجۡرَهُم بِأَحۡسَنِ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
16:96.en: That which ye have wasteth away, and that which Allah hath remaineth. And verily We shall pay those who are steadfast a recompense in proportion to the best of what they used to do

13:26.ar: ٱللَّهُ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقۡدِرُۚ وَفَرِحُواْ بِٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتَٰعࣱ‏
13:26.en: Allah enlargeth livelihood for whom He will, and straiteneth (it for whom He will); and they rejoice in the life of the world, whereas the life of the world is but brief comfort as compared with the Hereafter

4:77.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهُمۡ كُفُّوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَكُمۡ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ إِذَا فَرِيقࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ يَخۡشَوۡنَ ٱلنَّاسَ كَخَشۡيَةِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡ أَشَدَّ خَشۡيَةࣰۚ وَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَا لِمَ كَتَبۡتَ عَلَيۡنَا ٱلۡقِتَالَ لَوۡلَآ أَخَّرۡتَنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ قَرِيبࣲۗ قُلۡ مَتَٰعُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا قَلِيلࣱ وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ خَيۡرࣱ لِّمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ وَلَا تُظۡلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا
4:77.en: Hast thou not seen those unto whom it was said: Withhold your hands, establish worship and pay the poordue, but when fighting was prescribed for them behold! a party of them fear mankind even as their fear of Allah or with greater fear, and say: Our Lord! Why hast Thou ordained fighting for us? If only Thou wouldst give us respite yet a while! Say (unto them, O Muhammad): The comfort of this world is scant; the Hereafter will be better for him who wardeth off (evil); and ye will not be wronged the down upon a date-stone

20:131.ar: وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيۡنَيۡكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعۡنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ زَهۡرَةَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لِنَفۡتِنَهُمۡ فِيهِۚ وَرِزۡقُ رَبِّكَ خَيۡرࣱ وَأَبۡقَىٰ
20:131.en: And strain not thine eyes toward that which We cause some wedded pairs among them to enjoy, the flower of the life of the world, that We may try them thereby. The provision of thy Lord is better and more lasting

93:4.en: And verily the latter portion will be better for thee than the former

93:5.en: And verily thy Lord will give unto thee so that thou wilt be content

3:139.ar: وَلَا تَهِنُواْ وَلَا تَحۡزَنُواْ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡأَعۡلَوۡنَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
3:139.en: Faint not nor grieve, for ye will overcome them if ye are (indeed) believers

4:104.ar: وَلَا تَهِنُواْ فِي ٱبۡتِغَآءِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِۖ إِن تَكُونُواْ تَأۡلَمُونَ فَإِنَّهُمۡ يَأۡلَمُونَ كَمَا تَأۡلَمُونَۖ وَتَرۡجُونَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَرۡجُونَۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا
4:104.en: Relent not in pursuit of the enemy. If ye are suffering, lo! they suffer even as ye suffer and ye hope from Allah that for which they cannot hope. Allah is ever Knower, Wise

47:35.ar: فَلَا تَهِنُواْ وَتَدۡعُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلسَّلۡمِ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡأَعۡلَوۡنَ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَكُمۡ وَلَن يَتِرَكُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلَكُمۡ
47:35.en: So do not falter and cry out for peace when ye (will be) the uppermost, and Allah is with you, and He will not grudge (the reward of) your actions

8:60.ar: وَأَعِدُّواْ لَهُم مَّا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُم مِّن قُوَّةࣲ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ ٱلۡخَيۡلِ تُرۡهِبُونَ بِهِۦ عَدُوَّ ٱللَّهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمۡ وَءَاخَرِينَ مِن دُونِهِمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُهُمۡۚ وَمَا تُنفِقُواْ مِن شَيۡءࣲ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ يُوَفَّ إِلَيۡكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تُظۡلَمُونَ
8:60.en: Make ready for them all thou canst of (armed) force and of horses tethered, that thereby ye may dismay the enemy of Allah and your enemy, and others beside them whom ye know not. Allah knoweth them. Whatsoever ye spend in the way of Allah it will be repaid to you in full, and ye will not be wronged

33:28.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٰجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَزِينَتَهَا فَتَعَالَيۡنَ أُمَتِّعۡكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحۡكُنَّ سَرَاحࣰ ا جَمِيلࣰ ا
33:28.en: O Prophet! Say unto thy wives: If ye desire the world's life and its adornment, come! I will content you and will release you with a fair release

33:29.ar: وَإِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلۡمُحۡسِنَٰتِ مِنكُنَّ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
33:29.en: But if ye desire Allah and His messenger and the abode of the Hereafter, then lo! Allah hath prepared for the good among you an immense reward

lYxxKxJGIPY.speaker: adnan
lYxxKxJGIPY.speaker_note: 10th in his 'Achieving the Balance' series, comments on extremes he sees in his own community
lYxxKxJGIPY.title: Achieving the Balance: Asceticism and Wealth
lYxxKxJGIPY.one_line: The Prophet lived simply by choice, but asceticism is not poverty: Muslims must become strong and wealthy, then use it to serve.
lYxxKxJGIPY.summary: The tenth balance khutbah begins with the agreed part: zuhd is one of the Prophet's most visible traits and the Quran repeatedly calls worldly enjoyment brief and tells the Prophet not to look longingly at what others have. Aisha described months without a cooking fire, the Prophet's mat left marks on his body, he likened himself to a traveller resting under a tree, he died with his armour pawned, and companions pledged to take from the world only a traveller's provision. Then the balance: asceticism and poverty are not the same, and confusing them is a modern Muslim problem. The Prophet worked from childhood and was never poor after fifteen; his simple life was a choice, as he gave everything away, so much that his wives objected and the Quran gave them a choice. The Quran says not to be weak, to prepare strength, and that the giving hand is better, and the strong believer is more beloved to Allah. He urges parents to raise children to be as strong and wealthy as possible in every field, because whoever abandons the world leaves it to others. Wealth should be in your hand, not your heart. He criticizes both community extremes: people who sit in the masjid unable to make ends meet, and people too consumed by work to attend Jumuah.

outline.heading: The tenth balance
outline.gist: Each talk in the series states an undisputed Islamic value, then the caveat needed to understand it in balance; without both sides Muslims misread what Allah is explaining.

outline.heading: Simplicity: the Prophet's most visible trait
outline.gist: Watched from afar, even by someone who knew little of the deen, what stands out is that he chose to live simply, and the Quran pushes the same.

outline.heading: Worldly joy is brief
outline.gist: People rejoice in this life, yet it is only a few moments of enjoyment; the Hereafter is better for the God-fearing, and no one will be wronged.

outline.heading: Do not extend your eyes
outline.gist: He was told not to gaze at the splendour given to others and to be content, since what awaits is better and he will be given until satisfied.

outline.heading: A month without a cooking fire
outline.gist: Aisha said he never had bread with oil twice in a day, and a month would pass with no fire lit in their house, living on dates and water.

outline.heading: A traveller resting under a tree
outline.gist: His coarse mat left its pattern on his body; offered something softer, he said he was like a traveller who rests in a tree's shade and moves on.

outline.heading: The provision of a traveller
outline.gist: Companions pledged to take from the world only a traveller's provision, a phrase repeated in eight or nine narrations, and later felt they had fallen short though they owned almost nothing.

outline.heading: He died with his shield in pawn
outline.gist: He had pawned his shield with a neighbour for a loan to help someone else, and left nothing in wealth to divide, only his teaching for everyone.

outline.heading: The agreed part, in Arabic
outline.gist: He restates the first half, on the Prophet's simple life, in Arabic.

outline.heading: Asceticism is not poverty
outline.gist: No one disputes the Prophet's simplicity, but zuhd and being poor are not the same, and treating them as equal is a problem for Muslims today.

outline.heading: Never poor after fifteen
outline.gist: He worked from the age of eight, was trading by fifteen and always had more than enough; his lifestyle was a choice, not something forced on him.

outline.heading: Neither the Quran nor the Prophet encourages weakness
outline.gist: Accepting poverty with no ambition differs from choosing simplicity; Muslims are encouraged to be wealthy and strong, and the question becomes what the wealth is for.

outline.heading: Do not be weak; prepare all the strength you can
outline.gist: The Quran says 'do not be weak' three times and commands preparing every strength you can, which assumes you have something to prepare.

outline.heading: The upper hand is better
outline.gist: The giving hand is always better than the receiving one; start with your dependents, and the best charity comes from someone with surplus.

outline.heading: The strong believer is more beloved
outline.gist: Strength of any kind, academic, social, financial, political or physical, is what the deen encourages; then live simply with it.

outline.heading: He never cashed in
outline.gist: From fifteen to sixty-three he gave away whatever he earned and never said 'now it is my turn', which is almost impossible for anyone else.

outline.heading: His wives were given a choice
outline.gist: He gave away everything, even hundreds of sheep, until his wives objected and the Quran gave them the choice to leave with wealth or stay with his way of life. The richest companions also lived simply, because zuhd was a choice.

outline.heading: Neither extreme, in Arabic
outline.gist: Wealth is meant to serve Allah and His ummah, and neither extreme is acceptable; he then restates the balance in Arabic.

outline.heading: If you leave the dunya, who are you leaving it to?
outline.gist: Young Muslims are commanded to be strong, powerful and wealthy; the rich never give their wealth away, and money buys almost everything, even consciences and countries.

outline.heading: Without wealth there would be no Islam
outline.gist: The companions' wealth built the army and the state; wealth is for serving Allah, lifting people from poverty and strengthening the ummah, so we need entrepreneurs and business owners.

outline.heading: In your hand, not your heart
outline.gist: You own your car; it does not own you. If losing something would break you, it owns you; zuhd means nothing in the world owns you.

outline.heading: Teach your children to be strong in every field
outline.gist: Raise children to be as strong and wealthy as possible in every discipline, then to use it as the Prophet did.

outline.heading: Khadija's testimony: his wealth carried others
outline.gist: When he came down the mountain afraid, Khadija listed how he carried those who could not carry themselves; even before prophethood his money served others and he refused to be owned by his possessions.

outline.heading: Those who leave the world behind
outline.gist: A nice car, house and travel are fine, but a Muslim is not allowed to be weak; some in the community have left the world and can barely make a living, thinking this is how to live.

outline.heading: Those the world has consumed
outline.gist: He tells the first group to find a job and come to the masjid for one prayer, since weakness helps no one; the opposite group is so consumed by work they barely make Jumuah. Both fall short of the Prophet.

outline.heading: Umar and the man reading Quran
outline.gist: Finding a man reading Quran at work hours while his brother supported him, Umar said the brother was the greater worshipper.

outline.heading: Real devotion walks with strength
outline.gist: Aisha saw men walking weakly and asked if they were ill; told they were devout worshippers, she said Umar was more devout and walked with strength.

outline.heading: Why do you want wealth?
outline.gist: To enjoy it yourself or to serve others with it: the question he repeats four times, because zuhd and strength are both known and must be brought together.

outline.heading: Second khutbah in Arabic
outline.gist: The second khutbah, given in Arabic.

36:13.ar: وَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُم مَّثَلًا أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ إِذۡ جَآءَهَا ٱلۡمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:13.en: Coin for them a similitude: The people of the city when those sent (from Allah) came unto them

36:14.ar: إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡهِمُ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزۡنَا بِثَالِثࣲ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُم مُّرۡسَلُونَ
36:14.en: When We sent unto them twain, and they denied them both, so We reinforced them with a third, and they said: Lo! we have been sent unto you

36:15.ar: قَالُواْ مَآ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا بَشَرࣱ مِّثۡلُنَا وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا تَكۡذِبُونَ
36:15.en: They said: Ye are but mortals like unto us. The Beneficent hath naught revealed. Ye do but lie

36:16.ar: قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا يَعۡلَمُ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُمۡ لَمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:16.en: They answered: Our Lord knoweth that we are indeed sent unto you

36:17.en: And our duty is but plain conveyance (of the message)

36:18.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا تَطَيَّرۡنَا بِكُمۡۖ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهُواْ لَنَرۡجُمَنَّكُمۡ وَلَيَمَسَّنَّكُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
36:18.en: (The people of the city) said: We augur ill of you. If ye desist not, we shall surely stone you, and grievous torture will befall you at our hands

36:19.ar: قَالُواْ طَٰٓئِرُكُم مَّعَكُمۡ أَئِن ذُكِّرۡتُمۚ بَلۡ أَنتُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ مُّسۡرِفُونَ
36:19.en: They said: Your evil augury be with you! Is it because ye are reminded (of the truth)? Nay, but ye are froward folk

36:20.ar: وَجَآءَ مِنۡ أَقۡصَا ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ رَجُلࣱ يَسۡعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ
36:20.en: And there came from the uttermost part of the city a man running. He cried: O my people! Follow those who have been sent

36:21.ar: ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَن لَّا يَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ أَجۡرࣰ ا وَهُم مُّهۡتَدُونَ
36:21.en: Follow those who ask of you no fee, and who are rightly guided

36:22.ar: وَمَالِيَ لَآ أَعۡبُدُ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنِي وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
36:22.en: For what cause should I not serve Him Who hath created me, and unto Whom ye will be brought back

36:23.ar: ءَأَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةً إِن يُرِدۡنِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ بِضُرࣲّ لَّا تُغۡنِ عَنِّي شَفَٰعَتُهُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يُنقِذُونِ
36:23.en: Shall I take (other) gods in place of Him when, if the Beneficent should wish me any harm, their intercession will avail me naught, nor can they save

36:24.ar: إِنِّيٓ إِذࣰ ا لَّفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينٍ
36:24.en: Then truly I should be in error manifest

36:25.en: Lo! I have believed in your Lord, so hear me

36:26.ar: قِيلَ ٱدۡخُلِ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۖ قَالَ يَٰلَيۡتَ قَوۡمِي يَعۡلَمُونَ
36:26.en: It was said (unto him): Enter paradise. He said: Would that my people knew

36:27.ar: بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُكۡرَمِينَ
36:27.en: With what (munificence) my Lord hath pardoned me and made me of the honoured ones

36:3.en: Lo! thou art of those sent

36:5.en: A revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful

36:6.ar: لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمࣰ ا مَّآ أُنذِرَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ فَهُمۡ غَٰفِلُونَ
36:6.en: That thou mayst warn a folk whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless

36:7.ar: لَقَدۡ حَقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَىٰٓ أَكۡثَرِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
36:7.en: Already hath the judgment, (for their infidelity) proved true of most of them, for they believe not

36:8.ar: إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا فِيٓ أَعۡنَٰقِهِمۡ أَغۡلَٰلࣰ ا فَهِيَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَذۡقَانِ فَهُم مُّقۡمَحُونَ
36:8.en: Lo! We have put on their necks carcans reaching unto the chins, so that they are made stiff-necked

36:9.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنۢ بَيۡنِ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ سَدࣰّ ا وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ سَدࣰّ ا فَأَغۡشَيۡنَٰهُمۡ فَهُمۡ لَا يُبۡصِرُونَ
36:9.en: And We have set a bar before them and a bar behind them, and (thus) have covered them so that they see not

36:10.ar: وَسَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَأَنذَرۡتَهُمۡ أَمۡ لَمۡ تُنذِرۡهُمۡ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
36:10.en: Whether thou warn them or thou warn them not, it is alike for them, for they believe not

36:11.ar: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَخَشِيَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ فَبَشِّرۡهُ بِمَغۡفِرَةࣲ وَأَجۡرࣲ كَرِيمٍ
36:11.en: Thou warnest only him who followeth the Reminder and feareth the Beneficent in secret. To him bear tidings of forgiveness and a rich reward

36:12.ar: إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ وَنَكۡتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُواْ وَءَاثَٰرَهُمۡۚ وَكُلَّ شَيۡءٍ أَحۡصَيۡنَٰهُ فِيٓ إِمَامࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
36:12.en: Lo! We it is Who bring the dead to life. We record that which they send before (them, and their footprints. And all things We have kept in a clear Register)

6:122.ar: أَوَمَن كَانَ مَيۡتࣰ ا فَأَحۡيَيۡنَٰهُ وَجَعَلۡنَا لَهُۥ نُورࣰ ا يَمۡشِي بِهِۦ فِي ٱلنَّاسِ كَمَن مَّثَلُهُۥ فِي ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ لَيۡسَ بِخَارِجࣲ مِّنۡهَاۚ كَذَٰلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
6:122.en: Is he who was dead and We have raised him unto life, and set for him a light wherein he walketh among men, as him whose similitude is in utter darkness whence he cannot emerge? Thus is their conduct made fairseeming for the disbelievers

57:16.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ يَأۡنِ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَن تَخۡشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمۡ لِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا نَزَلَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَطَالَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَمَدُ فَقَسَتۡ قُلُوبُهُمۡۖ وَكَثِيرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ
57:16.en: Is not the time ripe for the hearts of those who believe to submit to Allah's reminder and to the truth which is revealed, that they become not as those who received the scripture of old but the term was prolonged for them and so their hearts were hardened, and many of them are evil-livers

57:17.ar: ٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحۡيِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَاۚ قَدۡ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
57:17.en: Know that Allah quickeneth the earth after its death. We have made clear Our revelations for you, that haply ye may understand

18:22.ar: سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَٰثَةࣱ رَّابِعُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ وَيَقُولُونَ خَمۡسَةࣱ سَادِسُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ رَجۡمَۢا بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ وَيَقُولُونَ سَبۡعَةࣱ وَثَامِنُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡۚ قُل رَّبِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ بِعِدَّتِهِم مَّا يَعۡلَمُهُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱۗ فَلَا تُمَارِ فِيهِمۡ إِلَّا مِرَآءࣰ ظَٰهِرࣰ ا وَلَا تَسۡتَفۡتِ فِيهِم مِّنۡهُمۡ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:22.en: (Some) will say: They were three, their dog the fourth, and (some) say: Five, their dog the sixth, guessing at random; and (some) say: Seven, and their dog the eighth. Say (O Muhammad): My Lord is Best Aware of their number. None knoweth them save a few. So contend not concerning them except with an outward contending, and ask not any of them to pronounce concerning them

17:90.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ تَفۡجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَنۢبُوعًا
17:90.en: And they say: We will not put faith in thee till thou cause a spring to gush forth from the earth for us

17:91.ar: أَوۡ تَكُونَ لَكَ جَنَّةࣱ مِّن نَّخِيلࣲ وَعِنَبࣲ فَتُفَجِّرَ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرَ خِلَٰلَهَا تَفۡجِيرًا
17:91.en: Or thou have a garden of date-palms and grapes, and cause rivers to gush forth therein abundantly

17:92.ar: أَوۡ تُسۡقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَمَا زَعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡنَا كِسَفًا أَوۡ تَأۡتِيَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ قَبِيلًا
17:92.en: Or thou cause the heaven to fall upon us piecemeal, as thou hast pretended, or bring Allah and the angels as a warrant

17:93.ar: أَوۡ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيۡتࣱ مِّن زُخۡرُفٍ أَوۡ تَرۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيۡنَا كِتَٰبࣰ ا نَّقۡرَؤُهُۥۗ قُلۡ سُبۡحَانَ رَبِّي هَلۡ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرࣰ ا رَّسُولࣰ ا
17:93.en: Or thou have a house of gold; or thou ascend up into heaven, and even then we will put no faith in thine ascension till thou bring down for us a book that we can read. Say (O Muhammad): My Lord be Glorified! Am I aught save a mortal messenger

16:48.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ مِن شَيۡءࣲ يَتَفَيَّؤُاْ ظِلَٰلُهُۥ عَنِ ٱلۡيَمِينِ وَٱلشَّمَآئِلِ سُجَّدࣰ ا لِّلَّهِ وَهُمۡ دَٰخِرُونَ
16:48.en: Have they not observed all things that Allah hath created, how their shadows incline to the right and to the left, making prostration unto Allah, and they are lowly

29:20.ar: قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ بَدَأَ ٱلۡخَلۡقَۚ ثُمَّ ٱللَّهُ يُنشِئُ ٱلنَّشۡأَةَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
29:20.en: Say (O Muhammad): Travel in the land and see how He originated creation, then Allah bringeth forth the later growth. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things

30:20.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنۡ خَلَقَكُم مِّن تُرَابࣲ ثُمَّ إِذَآ أَنتُم بَشَرࣱ تَنتَشِرُونَ
30:20.en: And of His signs is this: He created you of dust, and behold you human beings, ranging widely

7:131.ar: فَإِذَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ قَالُواْ لَنَا هَٰذِهِۦۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةࣱ يَطَّيَّرُواْ بِمُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥٓۗ أَلَآ إِنَّمَا طَٰٓئِرُهُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:131.en: But whenever good befell them, they said: This is ours; and whenever evil smote them they ascribed it to the evil auspices of Moses and those with him. Surely their evil auspice was only with Allah. But most of them knew not

28:20.ar: وَجَآءَ رَجُلࣱ مِّنۡ أَقۡصَا ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ يَسۡعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلۡمَلَأَ يَأۡتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقۡتُلُوكَ فَٱخۡرُجۡ إِنِّي لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ
28:20.en: And a man came from the uttermost part of the city, running. He said: O Moses! Lo! the chiefs take counsel against thee to slay thee; therefor escape. Lo! I am of those who give thee good advice

5:105.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنفُسَكُمۡۖ لَا يَضُرُّكُم مَّن ضَلَّ إِذَا ٱهۡتَدَيۡتُمۡۚ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
5:105.en: O ye who believe! Ye have charge of your own souls. He who erreth cannot injure you if ye are rightly guided. Unto Allah ye will all return; and then He will inform you of what ye used to do

34:47.ar: قُلۡ مَا سَأَلۡتُكُم مِّنۡ أَجۡرࣲ فَهُوَ لَكُمۡۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدࣱ‏
34:47.en: Say: Whatever reward I might have asked of you is yours. My reward is the affair of Allah only. He is Witness over all things

KetIP_ve9ww.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Yasin, the Believer of the Town (36:13-27)
KetIP_ve9ww.one_line: The story of the believer in Surat Yasin: real life comes through obedience and calling to Allah, against superstition, apathy and paid religion.
KetIP_ve9ww.summary: The only story in Surat Yasin is the man who came running from the far end of the town, so it carries the surah's meaning: real life is the life of the soul, gained by obeying Allah and calling others to Him, while the heedless are the living dead. He warns against chasing details Allah left out, like the town's location. The people demanded miracles because familiarity blinded them to the wonders around them, including their own bodies. Their reply, 'we see an evil omen in you', leads him into a long critique of superstition: omens, misused istikharah, horoscopes and the inflation of jinn, magic and the evil eye that grows when a civilisation declines. Istikharah is for two equal options you have not yet decided between, not for waiting on signs. The believer's word 'ya qawmi' shows belonging and responsibility: even with three messengers present, he felt the religion was his to carry. Every Muslim either carries the concern of the deen or is a burden on it. 'Follow those who ask no wage' leads to a warning that money corrupts dawah, citing the great imams who took nothing. Killed, the man's first words were wishing his people knew, so his memory lives on while they are forgotten.

outline.heading: The only story in the surah carries its meaning
outline.gist: When a surah holds one story found nowhere else, read it with extra care because the surah's axis turns on it.

outline.heading: Obedience through dawah is what gives life
outline.gist: Yasin, within the section from Al-Ahzab to Az-Zumar on submission, defines life as more than biology: animals breathe and eat as we do.

outline.heading: Souls die and Allah revives them
outline.gist: A soul starved of Allah's love and of calling to Him dies, but as Allah revives the earth He revives hearts.

outline.heading: The heedless are the living dead
outline.gist: The opening of the surah describes ghaflah: the one who does not care at all, unreachable by any call.

outline.heading: Do not dwell on what Allah left out
outline.gist: The town's location is unknown and useless; like the number of the cave sleepers, such debates waste time.

outline.heading: Three messengers in one town
outline.gist: They declared openly that they were messengers and were called liars.

outline.heading: Demanding miracles out of over-familiarity
outline.gist: People seek the extraordinary because they stopped seeing the wonder in the ordinary; maturity means stepping back to see it.

outline.heading: The Quran points to signs already before you
outline.gist: Quraysh demanded springs and palaces; the Quran answered with creation, the shade and the origin of man.

outline.heading: The miracle of a single bodily function
outline.gist: A doctor can spend 25 years just understanding the kidneys; knowing this keeps you grateful.

outline.heading: The messengers restate their mission
outline.gist: Our duty is only clear delivery; this setup is needed to understand what the believer did.

outline.heading: Reciting 36:18-19 and full assimilation of nun
outline.gist: In 'la'in lam' the nun disappears completely into the lam.

outline.heading: What tatayyur is
outline.gist: Judging reality by something unrelated to it, like taking a stumble on the way to an interview as a sign.

outline.heading: Istikharah: only between two equal options
outline.gist: It is not for choosing between obedience and sin or for decisions already made; it declares to Allah that you want what brings you closer.

outline.heading: No waiting for signs after istikharah
outline.gist: The companions decided and relied on Allah; a flat tyre is a nail, not a message.

outline.heading: Declining civilisations sink into superstition
outline.gist: Muslims have inflated jinn, magic and the evil eye until no failure is ever our own fault.

outline.heading: Scapegoating as a tool to silence
outline.gist: Said to Musa, Nuh and others, and used in media today to stir hatred; then threats replace discussion.

outline.heading: 'Your omen is with you'
outline.gist: The messengers turned the omen back on the people themselves.

outline.heading: Israf: excess in everything
outline.gist: Excess is not only in money but in war, defiance and rejection; mothers still blame a bride for misfortune.

outline.heading: Muslims judge by evidence: no contagion, no omens
outline.gist: The Prophet rejected omens and loved optimism; even educated people now follow horoscopes.

outline.heading: Islam took us out of darkness; why return to it?
outline.gist: These people were dead in mind, rejecting messengers who called them to good.

outline.heading: Reciting 36:20-22
outline.gist: A man came running from the farthest part of the city.

outline.heading: Why 'from the farthest part' comes first
outline.gist: Word order stresses how far he came, unlike the similar verse in the story of Musa.

outline.heading: Every excuse to stay home
outline.gist: He lived on the edge, there were three prophets present and his people were backward, yet he came.

outline.heading: 'Ya qawmi': belonging
outline.gist: He said follow the messengers, not me; his own teacher called 'my people' the most beautiful part of the story.

outline.heading: With no prophet among us, who is responsible?
outline.gist: If he felt responsible beside three messengers, how much more are we.

outline.heading: Carry the concern of the deen or be a burden on it
outline.gist: No one owns the religion more than another; extra knowledge only adds responsibility, and every Muslim is equally answerable.

outline.heading: You cannot detach from the ummah
outline.gist: 'Take care of yourselves' is no licence to abandon serving the community; Islam and that feeling cannot coexist.

outline.heading: Jealousy for the deen, and 'those who ask no wage'
outline.gist: Loving that Allah be obeyed brings real life; the prophets always said they wanted nothing from their people.

outline.heading: The great imams took no pay for teaching
outline.gist: Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafi'i and the hadith masters lived from their own work; Imam Ahmad gleaned leftover wheat.

outline.heading: Whoever pays you holds you captive
outline.gist: A teacher of the Quran must not be beholden to anyone or he will hold back the truth.

outline.heading: 'And they are rightly guided'
outline.gist: A caller must himself be upright or no one will listen.

outline.heading: 'Why should I not worship the One who created me'
outline.gist: Recitation of his argument against false gods.

outline.heading: Gods that cannot intercede or save
outline.gist: His reasoning with his people, and the elided ya' in 'yunqidhun' and 'fasma'un'.

outline.heading: His killing is passed over
outline.gist: Reports say they trampled him to death; the Quran skips straight to 'enter Paradise'.

outline.heading: 'Would that my people knew'
outline.gist: His first words after death were for the people who killed him: belonging at its highest.

outline.heading: Unnamed yet alive forever
outline.gist: His opponents are forgotten while he is recited till the Last Day; as al-Farazdaq said, not knowing a name does not harm its owner.

outline.heading: Life is not measured in years
outline.gist: Some live 20 years and are remembered for centuries; real death is seeing wrong and staying silent.

outline.heading: Prophets prayed for the people who hurt them
outline.gist: Wiping blood from his face, a prophet said 'forgive my people, for they do not know'.

MAEZinoDHWk.speaker: adnan
MAEZinoDHWk.speaker_note: his own Sunday tafseer halaqah concluding Surat ar-Rahman; brief audience questions answered
MAEZinoDHWk.title: Tafseer of Surat ar-Rahman: The Final Verses
MAEZinoDHWk.one_line: Concluding ar-Rahman: gratitude as Islamic maturity, the lower pair of gardens, hearts purified of jealousy, and the last man to leave Hell.
MAEZinoDHWk.summary: He recaps the cluster of surahs from Qaf to al-Hadid as a series of choices and presents ar-Rahman's choice as gratitude versus losing one's blessings, asked again and again by its refrain. Humans quickly take blessings for granted, so he defines Islamic maturity as growing sensitivity to what Allah has given, which shapes how one prays and speaks to Him. Our debt is infinite, but like an athlete trailing badly we should still give our best, because Allah answers excellence with His own. Turning to verses 62 onward, he reads the second pair of gardens as a rank slightly below the first, matching the Quran's three groups. No one in Paradise resents a higher rank, because jealousy and arrogance rest on illusions that are stripped away before entry, illustrated by Abdullah ibn Rawahah's slightly lower rank after a moment's hesitation at Mu'tah. Life, he says, is either gratitude or perseverance. He compares the wording of the two descriptions, from dark green foliage to gushing springs, then the fruits, exclusive spouses and incomparable furnishings. The hadith of the last man to leave Hell shows insatiable human desire, which should be redirected toward Paradise through a selfless path. The surah ends with the blessed name of the Lord, and its unanswered question will return as the record we write.

outline.heading: The short, comprehensive surahs
outline.gist: The final quarter is short yet comprehensive and focused on values and principles rather than rulings, ideal for those who struggle to memorize.

outline.heading: The cluster of choices
outline.gist: From Qaf onward each surah sets a choice: righteousness, purpose, guidance, knowledge over whims, and use of blessings.

outline.heading: Ar-Rahman: gratitude or loss
outline.gist: The refrain asks over thirty times which favours we deny; the first and greatest blessing is that our Lord is ar-Rahman.

outline.heading: We take blessings for granted
outline.gist: Humans stop noticing whatever is always there, which is why children seldom appreciate their parents' provision; zooming out has to be taught.

outline.heading: Blessings everyone shares
outline.gist: The surah lists universal blessings: being made from clay, the two seas, ships that float, even death and accountability.

outline.heading: Islamic maturity is sensitivity to blessings
outline.gist: Maturity is seeing ever more of what one has been given; prayer and khushu reflect how one views Allah's generosity.

outline.heading: You could have been anything
outline.gist: We had no say in being created as we are and own nothing to object with; revelation and intellect are given so life is worth living.

outline.heading: An infinite debt and the athlete's grit
outline.gist: We cannot repay Allah and have often walked the opposite way, but like a player ten goals down we keep giving our best.

outline.heading: Even Hell is a blessing
outline.gist: That oppressors and abusers cannot escape justice is itself a mercy.

outline.heading: Recap: two gardens and the reward of excellence
outline.gist: Those who fear standing before their Lord receive two gardens meeting every desire; give Allah your best and see His best.

outline.heading: Answering a question: whose excellence comes first
outline.gist: An attendee suggests Allah has already shown His excellence and now awaits ours; he accepts it as an equally profound reading.

outline.heading: 'Besides these, two more gardens'
outline.gist: Read as one degree below; the Quran regularly divides people into three groups, two of whom succeed.

outline.heading: No jealousy or arrogance enters Paradise
outline.gist: Diseases of the heart must be purified first; jealousy rests on illusions that vanish when one sees Hell brought forth on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Certainty and love for those ranked higher
outline.gist: Everyone's iman becomes certain when experienced directly; seeing someone ranked higher by Allah brings love, not resentment.

outline.heading: Abdullah ibn Rawahah's moment of hesitation
outline.gist: The Prophet described Zayd, Ja'far and Ibn Rawahah in Paradise, the last slightly lower for an inner hesitation at Mu'tah no one else saw; every detail is weighed.

outline.heading: Life is gratitude or perseverance
outline.gist: Use what you have in service, or persevere toward what you lack; picture perseverance as climbing a mountain at night in wind and rain.

outline.heading: Dark green gardens
outline.gist: Where the first gardens have many branches, these are so green they look black: abundant options, less sharply defined.

outline.heading: Gushing springs versus flowing ones
outline.gist: Flowing water is more peaceful than gushing water; the word choices mark the difference in rank.

outline.heading: Grateful even for what we dislike
outline.gist: The alternative to everything is nothingness, humanity's deepest fear; even death is a blessing that motivates action.

outline.heading: Recitation note: elongation counts
outline.gist: The six-count madd followed by two counts for the doubled nun when pausing.

outline.heading: Fruits, palms and pomegranates
outline.gist: Naming a few fruits signals plenty but less variety than the first gardens; the repeated question keeps pressing for an answer.

outline.heading: Good and beautiful companions in pavilions
outline.gist: Exclusive intimacy answers the human need to be wanted by one person; it applies to both men and women.

outline.heading: Answering a question on jinn and the companions
outline.gist: He understands these as beings Allah creates in Paradise for its people, not humans made the object of others' pleasure.

outline.heading: Green cushions and incomparable carpets
outline.gist: Abqari describes something unmatched, hence its use for a genius; the furnishings exceed anything imagined.

outline.heading: The last man to leave Hell
outline.gist: Restored in the river of life, he asks for one tree, then a better one, then another, each time promising to ask for no more.

outline.heading: The black hole of desire
outline.gist: Wanting more is human and not wrong, but worldly consumption only deepens the emptiness, which is why the well-off reach for pills.

outline.heading: Be selfish for Paradise by being selfless here
outline.gist: The only way to satisfy that ultimate selfishness is a path of selflessness, compassion and responsibility for others.

outline.heading: Ten times the greatest kingdom
outline.gist: Finding Paradise full, he is offered the dominion of the greatest king and then tenfold, and that is the lowest rank.

outline.heading: The highest see their Lord
outline.gist: The highest ranks care only for meeting Allah, the source of all beauty, which they do twice a day.

outline.heading: Blessed is the name of your Lord
outline.gist: The surah begins with the name ar-Rahman and ends with His blessed name as the source of all barakah.

outline.heading: The unanswered question returns
outline.gist: The refrain fades without an answer but will return on the Day of Judgment, answered by the record we write now.

themes.label: Gratitude and recognizing blessings
themes.note: Islamic maturity is growing sensitivity to Allah's blessings; our debt is infinite yet we must give our best.

themes.label: Excellence answered with excellence
themes.note: Give Allah your best and He gives His; or, He has shown His best and awaits ours.

themes.label: The ranks and gardens of Paradise
themes.note: A second pair of gardens one degree lower, described through deliberate shifts of wording, and the lowest and highest ranks of Paradise.

themes.label: Jealousy purified before Paradise
themes.note: Jealousy and arrogance rest on illusions and cannot enter Paradise; there people love those ranked above them.

themes.label: Perseverance as climbing
themes.note: Life is gratitude for what you have or perseverance toward what you lack, imagined as climbing a mountain in a storm.

themes.label: Nothingness and death as blessing
themes.note: The fear of nothingness shows existence is a blessing; death gives life urgency.

themes.label: Insatiable desire and selflessness
themes.note: Worldly desire is a black hole; direct the wish for more toward Paradise, reached only through selflessness.

themes.label: The blessed name of the Lord
themes.note: The surah opens and closes on His name as the source of every blessing.

quran.point: People are divided into three groups, two of which succeed.
Allah removes rancour from the hearts of the people of Paradise.

hadith.gist: No one with an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise.
Hell is brought forth on the Day of Judgment with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels.
During the battle of Mu'tah the Prophet described the three commanders' deaths and saw them in Paradise, Ibn Rawahah slightly lower for a moment's hesitation.
The last man to leave Hell is restored in a river of life, asks for tree after tree, and is finally given ten times the dominion of the greatest king.
The highest people of Paradise look upon their Lord morning and evening.

maxims: Islamic maturity is sensitivity to blessings
Give Him your best and see His best
There's no third option: gratitude or perseverance
Be selfish for Paradise, selfless on the way
Jealousy is based on an illusion

stories.point: Even an unseen moment of hesitation is weighed and affects rank.

takeaways: Make a habit of noticing and thanking Allah for basic, shared blessings

fcZmDzgi34M.speaker: adnan
fcZmDzgi34M.speaker_note: part of his 'Achieving the Balance' series; apologizes on behalf of himself and other speakers
fcZmDzgi34M.title: Achieving the Balance: The Intellect and the Heart
fcZmDzgi34M.one_line: Islam is built on reason and evidence, but faith held only in the mind rusts; the heart must follow the intellect into love and tears.
fcZmDzgi34M.summary: This balance khutbah first establishes the undisputed point: Islam is a religion of logic and evidence. The Quran repeatedly demands proof from its opponents, calls idols mere names with no authority, says assumption is no substitute for truth, and ends verse after verse urging reflection. Tawhid is the simplest explanation of existence, and the Arabs rejected it not because it made no sense but because it ended corruption and profit; a person of tawhid becomes dangerous to anything irrational. Blindness is of hearts, not eyes, and people who do not use their minds are worse than cattle. Even a mistaken jurist is rewarded for sound reasoning, and superstition and amulets were removed so the community could think. The balance: no one can sustain faith with the intellect alone. Without the heart, belief slowly rusts. He cites the sweetness of faith found in loving Allah and His Prophet most, the companions' tears, Hanzala fearing he was a hypocrite, Abu Bakr weeping too much to lead prayer, and the verse about skins shivering at the Quran. He apologizes that speakers like him often fail to reach hearts, warns that emotion-only faith is a ticking bomb, and notes the companions remembered the feeling more than the words.

outline.heading: A nation of moderation
outline.gist: Each talk in the series states an agreed concept, then the exceptions needed to understand and practise it properly, aiming at the nation of moderation Allah describes.

outline.heading: A religion of reason
outline.gist: Muslims have not done well at balance in recent decades; the agreed point today is that the deen rests on logic and the human intellect, and its simplicity is what draws people to it.

outline.heading: Bring your proof
outline.gist: The Quran keeps telling opponents to bring their evidence, even saying that if the Most Merciful had a son, the Prophet would be the first to worship.

outline.heading: Names you made up
outline.gist: Idols are names invented by people and their forefathers with no authority; they follow assumption and desire, and assumption is no substitute for the truth.

outline.heading: So that you may reflect
outline.gist: Verse after verse ends hoping we will reflect and understand, because people easily follow beliefs that make no sense; tawhid is the simplest concept there is.

outline.heading: Tawhid explains everything
outline.gist: One source explains why everything works the same way from the atom to the galaxy; the Arabs rejected it not because it made no sense but because it closed the doors to corruption.

outline.heading: Tawhid isn't lucrative
outline.gist: Without idols, clergy could not sell rulings or control people; a servant of Allah alone becomes dangerous, refusing anything irrational or corrupt.

outline.heading: Hearts go blind, not eyes
outline.gist: It is the inner faculty that goes blind, not the eyes; the world is full of people who cannot see yet have insight.

outline.heading: Worse than cattle
outline.gist: Those with minds, eyes and ears they never use are like livestock or worse, since cattle have no choice; there is no cure for indifference. Look at what you were created from and at your food.

outline.heading: The mistaken jurist is still rewarded
outline.gist: A jurist who reaches the right ruling gets two rewards and a wrong one gets one, because his reasoning was sound; sound logic cannot be faulted.

outline.heading: Superstition was removed
outline.gist: Charms, fairy tales and carrying objects for protection were abolished, because a community rises only when it starts thinking properly.

outline.heading: The agreed part, in Arabic
outline.gist: He calls this point undisputed and restates it in Arabic.

outline.heading: The mind cannot carry faith alone
outline.gist: No Muslim can continue the journey with only the intellect invested; you believe because it is the simplest explanation, but the heart must be at the same level.

outline.heading: Without the heart, belief rusts
outline.gist: Belief settled by the mind slowly rusts and fades if the heart does not come along; if you love Allah, follow the Prophet, and Allah will bring a people He loves and who love Him.

outline.heading: The sweetness of faith
outline.gist: Three things bring it: loving Allah and His Prophet above all, loving others only for Allah, and hating to leave the faith as one hates being thrown into fire.

outline.heading: Eyes filled with tears
outline.gist: Companions report again and again that when the Prophet admonished them their eyes flowed and their hearts trembled.

outline.heading: Hanzala: 'I have become a hypocrite'
outline.gist: Hanzala lost the feeling at home among his family and animals and feared hypocrisy; Abu Bakr felt the same. Their hearts were moved because the mind had already settled, so the two agreed without forcing tears.

outline.heading: Emotion-only faith collapses
outline.gist: Faith entered only through emotion, without understanding, comes crashing down when the winds blow; it must start with the intellect, and then the heart must follow.

ASNa7PFmAe4.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Waqi'ah, Part 1: Verses 1-19
ASNa7PFmAe4.one_line: Al-Waqi'ah 1-19: the inevitable Event reshuffles all status, strips everything physical away, and sorts people into three groups.
ASNa7PFmAe4.summary: Al-Waqi'ah continues the cluster of surahs that pose life's biggest choices, asking which of three groups you want to be in on the Day of Judgment. The Event is described in the past tense because to Allah it has as good as happened, and no one can deny it. It lowers and raises: worldly status built on wealth, lineage, colour, titles and fame is reshuffled, the arrogant are raised the size of ants, and value is judged by what was in the heart. The earth is violently shaken and mountains crumble to scattered dust, so nothing physical is left: no home, possessions, phone or supplier, as the pandemic's empty shelves hinted. Only the inner self remains, and deeds take form beside their owner. People become three groups: the fortunate, the wretched and the forerunners brought near, many from earlier generations but few from later ones. He links that to the Prophet's warning that he feared abundance of this world, not poverty, for his ummah, and to wealth used without gratitude. The odds of two good groups out of three favour us, but the decisive choices come quietly, without any dramatic music, and can be made right now. He closes with the forerunners' jewelled couches, immortal youths serving them and drink without headache, urging people to serve in this life and to remember the choice is theirs.

outline.heading: A beloved surah in a cluster of life's big choices
outline.gist: The surahs from Qaf onward each pose a question: righteousness or falsehood, purpose or aimlessness, gratitude or ingratitude; Al-Waqi'ah asks which of three people you will be.

outline.heading: A simple surah that begins and ends with three groups
outline.gist: One of the most straightforward themes in the Quran; he then recites the opening.

outline.heading: Al-Waqi'ah: the reality that falls into place
outline.gist: Waqi' is reality as it is; the Event slowly tilts toward the moment it lands and becomes the only thing that is.

outline.heading: The future told in the past tense
outline.gist: Allah speaks of what will happen as if it already has, because His word needs no waiting.

outline.heading: No soul can deny its occurrence
outline.gist: Believe it or not, protest or not, it is coming; figure out where you will be.

outline.heading: This world's measures of status
outline.gist: Background, wealth, education, politics, gender, colour all feed a complicated metric of who is high and low.

outline.heading: It lowers and raises: the metric changes
outline.gist: Lineage, looks, bank balance and the letters around your name stop mattering; there are only three slots.

outline.heading: The arrogant raised the size of ants
outline.gist: People who had crowds waiting for them will be trampled; fame is not evil, but it is not where value comes from.

outline.heading: Judged by what was in the heart
outline.gist: Intentions, hopes, selflessness, trustworthiness and honesty are all that will be weighed.

outline.heading: Resurrected unable even to cover yourself
outline.gist: No connections or workarounds remain; only merit in Allah's eyes.

outline.heading: The mask ripped away
outline.gist: The image we build is torn off and we stand exposed if there was no substance behind it.

outline.heading: Bounties we can never repay
outline.gist: Sight, hearing, safety from war and dictators have no price; all that is left is dedicating your life to pleasing Him.

outline.heading: Iqlab: noon becomes meem before ba
outline.gist: A tajweed note on the small meem above the noon.

outline.heading: The earth shaken violently
outline.gist: Rajj is shaking to the point of breaking; the verbal noun after the verb signals it happens to the fullest extent.

outline.heading: Mountains crumbled to pieces
outline.gist: Bass is crumbling into small bits; the world as we know it is gone.

outline.heading: Nothing physical is left
outline.gist: No home, clothes, phone or store; like children who think chickens come from Costco, we assumed supplies were endless until the pandemic's empty shelves.

outline.heading: Scattered dust and nowhere to go
outline.gist: Haba' munbath is particles too fine to gather; no call to make, no bus to wait for, as hard to grasp as infinity.

outline.heading: Only what is inside remains
outline.gist: Everything we use to cover who we are is removed; deeds and morals take physical form and follow their owner.

outline.heading: What is left of you?
outline.gist: Allah looks at hearts and deeds, not bodies; titles and possessions are erased, so work on why you do what you do.

outline.heading: Three groups: the bottom line of the human story
outline.gist: A very long, complex story ends in three groups of humans and jinn, and each of us must work out which we will be in.

outline.heading: The fortunate, the wretched and the forerunners
outline.gist: The rhetorical question builds desire for the first and dread of the second; repeating 'the forerunners' says words cannot describe them.

outline.heading: Brought near: many from the early, few from the later
outline.gist: Thullah is a share by percentage; the earlier nations supplied a larger share of the forerunners.

outline.heading: Pioneers who refuse mediocrity
outline.gist: A companion prayed to be among the few, since few servants are grateful; forerunners saw the opportunity and chose to excel.

outline.heading: Two out of three: the odds are in your favour
outline.gist: Only one group is a problem; just make sure you are not in the third.

outline.heading: Big decisions come without background music
outline.gist: Life has no dramatic soundtrack; many decisive choices are already made and another can be made right now, seen only by you and Allah.

outline.heading: Our appointment is at the Basin
outline.gist: Too busy to accept invitations, the Prophet told companions to meet him at the Hawd, where some will be called near and others turned away.

outline.heading: Why fewer from the later: 'I do not fear poverty for you'
outline.gist: When wealth came from Bahrain, the Prophet told the poor he feared abundance of this world would ruin them as it ruined those before.

outline.heading: Too much and too little gratitude
outline.gist: The rich who give everywhere outrank others, as the poor companions learned when the wealthy copied their dhikr; with great wealth comes great responsibility.

outline.heading: Jewelled couches facing one another
outline.gist: Thrones studded with gems; the forerunners recline in the company of the great names they only read about.

outline.heading: Immortal youths serve them
outline.gist: Learn to serve in this world so that you are served in the next; the servants are ever-young and eager.

outline.heading: Drink without headache or intoxication
outline.gist: What you gave up in this world for Allah is returned better and lasting, with no price at the end.

outline.heading: Your group is your choice
outline.gist: Read the coming verses, especially the third page; this is not predestined against you, Allah gave you the choice.
